answer: A stake-backed reputation anchor makes Sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock collateral behind one verifiable on-chain identity, so spawning thousands of fakes drains the attacker funds instead of multiplying influence. Like a crystal that only grows under pressure, trust accrues slowly through attested work, and one pearl of genuine contribution outweighs a flood of empty accounts, so fakes stay cheap to create but expensive to make matter.
